field.label: Active (Use this Server)
field.help: Enable this outbound server node.

field.label: Node Name / Remarks
field.help: Friendly name for this server (automatically extracted from #remark when importing vless:// links).

field.label: Protocol
field.help: Outbound type. VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, SOCKS 5, HTTP, Hysteria 2 and MASQUE connect to a remote server; WireGuard is a tunnel; Freedom (Direct), Blackhole (Block), DNS and Loopback are built-in helpers. The fields below change with this choice.

field.label: Server Address (IP or Domain)
field.help: Hostname or IP address of the remote server this node connects to.

field.label: Server Port
field.help: Port of the remote server (usually 443).

field.label: UUID / Password
field.help: User UUID (VLESS/VMess) or Password (Trojan/Shadowsocks).

field.label: Username
field.help: Username for SOCKS, HTTP or MASQUE authentication. Leave empty when the server does not require auth.

field.label: Password
field.help: Password for SOCKS, HTTP or MASQUE authentication.

field.label: XTLS Flow
field.help: Flow control algorithm for VLESS (usually xtls-rprx-vision for REALITY/TLS).

field.label: Encryption
field.help: Keep as "none" for standard VLESS, or paste a VLESS Encryption string generated by "xray vlessenc".

field.label: Email
field.help: Email address for VLESS user identification.

field.label: Extra (VLESS)
field.help: VLESS user extra (encryption material, e.g. for ML-KEM VLESS encryption), as JSON. Transport XHTTP extras go to the "XHTTP Extra" field below. Imported from vless:// links only when type is not xhttp/splithttp.

field.label: Shadowsocks Cipher
field.help: Encryption method; it must match the server. The 2022-blake3 methods need a base64 key of the matching length (16 bytes for aes-128, 32 bytes for aes-256) in the password field.

field.label: VMess Encryption
field.help: Cipher for the VMess payload. auto picks AES-128-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 by CPU support; keep auto unless the server requires a specific one.

field.label: VMess Experiments
field.help: Optional experimental flags separated by "|", e.g. AuthenticatedLength|NoTerminationSignal.

field.label: Client Private Key
field.help: Client private key (PrivateKey generated by "xray wg").

field.label: Peer Public Key
field.help: Server public key (Password/PublicKey generated by "xray wg").

field.label: Pre-Shared Key (optional)
field.help: Optional symmetric key shared with the peer (base64) that adds an extra encryption layer. Leave empty unless the peer is configured with one.

field.label: Peer Endpoint (host:port)
field.help: Server address and port, e.g. example.com:51820.

field.label: Local Address(es)
field.help: Local IP addresses assigned inside the WireGuard tunnel (e.g. 10.0.0.1).

field.label: Allowed IPs
field.help: Destinations routed through the peer, usually 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0.

field.label: Persistent Keepalive (seconds)
field.help: 0 disables keepalive packets.

field.label: Inner MTU
field.help: Default 1420 (IPv6 endpoint) or 1440 (IPv4 endpoint).

field.label: Reserved Bytes
field.help: Three comma-separated bytes, e.g. 0,0,0.

field.label: Remote DNS Servers
field.help: DNS servers used inside the tunnel to resolve proxied domain names (IP addresses only).

field.label: Disable Kernel TUN (use gVisor)
field.help: Do not use the kernel TUN device even if it is available; Xray's built-in userspace network stack (gVisor) is used instead.

field.label: Redirect To (host:port)
field.help: Rewrite the destination, e.g. 127.0.0.1:3366. Use :443 to keep the address, host:0 to keep the port.

field.label: PROXY Protocol
field.help: Used together with Redirect when the backend supports the PROXY protocol.

field.label: Final Rules (JSON array)
field.help: Optional JSON array, e.g. [{"action":"block","network":"tcp","port":"25,465"}]. Leave empty to use the built-in safety policy.

field.label: Response
field.help: Close the connection immediately, or send a simple HTTP 403 response before closing.

field.label: Rewrite Transport
field.help: Transport used for DNS queries passing through this outbound: keep the original one, or force TCP or UDP.

field.label: Rewrite DNS Server Address
field.help: Leave empty to keep the address requested by the source.

field.label: Rewrite DNS Server Port
field.help: Leave empty to keep the port requested by the source.

field.label: DNS Rules (JSON array)
field.help: Optional JSON array, e.g. [{"action":"return","rCode":3,"domain":["domain:ads.example"]}].

field.label: Inbound Tag
field.help: Tag used when traffic re-enters routing. Avoid rules that send it back to this outbound.

field.label: Hysteria Auth Password
field.help: Must match the server. Hysteria always uses TLS transport.

field.label: UDP Idle Timeout (seconds)
field.help: Idle timeout for a single QUIC native UDP connection (default 60).

field.label: MASQUE Authority (:authority)
field.help: Optional CONNECT-IP :authority. Priority: host > SNI > server address.

field.label: MASQUE Path Template
field.help: RFC 9484 path, default /.well-known/masque/ip/{target}/{ipproto}/.

field.label: Remote DNS Servers
field.help: DNS servers used inside the MASQUE tunnel (IP addresses only).

field.label: Transport Network (type)
field.help: Transport method. Not used by WireGuard, Freedom, Blackhole, DNS and Loopback; Hysteria and MASQUE always use their native transport.

field.label: Stream Security
field.help: Hysteria and MASQUE always require TLS.

field.label: Server Name (SNI)
field.help: SNI hostname used during TLS/REALITY handshake.

field.label: uTLS Fingerprint (fp)
field.help: TLS client fingerprint Xray imitates (uTLS). chrome is a good default; change it only if the server or your network requires another one. Old Xray builds reject the newest names.

field.label: ALPN
field.help: Optional ALPN values (h2, http/1.1, h3, http/1.0). For MASQUE, h2 selects HTTP/2; otherwise HTTP/3 is used.

field.label: Verify Peer Cert By Name
field.help: Client-only. Hostname(s) used for certificate verification instead of SNI (comma-separated, wildcards allowed).

field.label: Pinned Peer Cert SHA-256
field.help: SHA-256 hex digest(s) of the peer certificate, comma-separated. Overrides normal certificate validation, so it also works with self-signed certificates and replaces Allow Insecure TLS. Produce the value with the xray tls hash or xray tls ping commands.

field.label: ECH Config List
field.help: ECH config: fixed Base64 string, or a DNS query URL like udp://1.1.1.1 / https://1.1.1.1/dns-query, optionally example.com+https://... .

field.label: Min TLS Version
field.help: Optional. One of: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. Leave empty for default.

field.label: Max TLS Version
field.help: Optional. One of: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. Leave empty for default.

field.label: Allow Insecure TLS
field.help: Skips server certificate verification. Deprecated by Xray-core and may be removed in a future release. Prefer Pinned Peer Cert SHA-256 below (the value can be produced with the xray tls hash or xray tls ping commands).

field.label: Use System CA Store
field.help: Trust the operating system's CA list instead of Xray's built-in one (Xray default: off). Useful when the server certificate is signed by a private CA that is installed on the router. Needs Xray-core 26.11.9 or newer; older cores ignore the option.

field.label: REALITY Public Key (pbk)
field.help: Public key of the REALITY server (pbk in share links). Required for REALITY.

field.label: REALITY ShortId (sid)
field.help: Short ID accepted by the REALITY server (sid in share links).

field.label: REALITY SpiderX (spx)
field.help: Initial path of the REALITY spider request (spx in share links). / is fine unless your server setup says otherwise.

field.label: REALITY ML-DSA-65 Verify Key
field.help: Optional. Post-quantum signature verification public key (xray mldsa65). Leave empty to disable.

field.label: Host Header / Authority
field.help: Host header (WebSocket, HTTPUpgrade, XHTTP). Usually the domain of the server; it must match what the server expects.

field.label: Path
field.help: Request path. It must start with / and match the server (for example /ws or /xhttp).

field.label: gRPC Service Name
field.help: gRPC service name; it must match the serviceName configured on the server.

field.label: gRPC MultiMode
field.help: gRPC multi mode (several packets per message). Enable it only if the server uses it too.

field.label: gRPC Authority
field.help: Optional HTTP/2 :authority for gRPC (can be used as a Host). Leave empty to use the server address.

field.label: gRPC User Agent
field.help: Client only. Custom User-Agent; may help against CDN blocks. Leave empty for default.

field.label: gRPC Idle Timeout (s)
field.help: Seconds of inactivity before a health check. Minimum effective 10. Empty = health checks disabled.

field.label: gRPC Health Check Timeout (s)
field.help: Seconds to wait for a health check response before considering it failed (default 20).

field.label: gRPC Permit Without Stream
field.help: Client only. Allow health checks when no streams are open.

field.label: gRPC Initial Windows Size
field.help: HTTP/2 stream initial window size. 0 disables (default). >65535 disables dynamic window.

field.label: XHTTP Mode
field.help: XHTTP mode. auto lets Xray choose; packet-up, stream-up and stream-one force one mode, which the server and any CDN in between must support.

field.label: XHTTP Extra (JSON object)
field.help: XHTTP transport extra (xhttpSettings.extra): headers, xPaddingBytes, scMaxEachPostBytes, scMinPostsIntervalMs, xmux, etc. On import, the 'extra' param of a vless:// link with type=xhttp/splithttp is placed here.

field.label: WebSocket Heartbeat Period (s)
field.help: Optional. Send a WebSocket Ping every N seconds. 0 or empty disables keepalive pings.

field.label: XDRIVE Storage
field.help: XDRIVE is a VLESS-only transport that tunnels through a cloud drive. Always requires VLESS encryption (run "xray vlessenc"), no flow, and Mux.Cool enabled with concurrency >= 0. For Google Drive also set TLS, a real Google IP, SNI www.google.com, ALPN h2 or h3, and fingerprint hellochrome_155 or chrome.

field.label: Remote Folder / Path
field.help: Google Drive folder ID, S3/template prefix, or a local folder path, depending on the storage.

field.label: Google OAuth Client ID
field.help: OAuth client ID of the Google Cloud project that owns the Drive folder.

field.label: Google OAuth Client Secret
field.help: OAuth client secret of the Google Cloud project used as the XDRIVE storage.

field.label: Google OAuth Refresh Token
field.help: Refresh token for the Google account; it is exchanged for access tokens at runtime.

field.label: S3 Endpoint URL
field.help: Full URL including scheme, e.g. https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com or https://minio.example.com:9000.

field.label: S3 Region
field.help: Optional. Defaults to us-east-1 when empty.

field.label: S3 Bucket
field.help: Name of the S3 bucket XDRIVE uses as the shared storage.

field.label: S3 Access Key ID
field.help: Access key ID with read/write access to the bucket.

field.label: S3 Secret Access Key
field.help: Secret access key for the bucket. It is stored in the plugin configuration.

field.label: S3 Session Token
field.help: Optional. Only for temporary STS credentials.

field.label: S3 Path-Style Addressing
field.help: Use endpoint/bucket/key instead of bucket.endpoint/key. Required by MinIO and most self-hosted S3 servers.

field.label: Template Secrets (JSON array)
field.help: JSON array of strings, available in the template as {secret0}, {secret1}, ... Example: ["token0","token1"].

field.label: Template (JSON object)
field.help: REST storage description: auth, put, get, list, delete operations. See the XDRIVE template documentation in Xray-core.

field.label: XDRIVE Extra (JSON object)
field.help: Optional tuning merged into xdriveSettings: segmentBytes, flushIntervalMs, pollIntervalMs, maxPollIntervalMs, sessionTtlSeconds, concurrency, eagerWindowMs, holeTimeoutMs, xmux. Example: {"concurrency":16,"xmux":{"maxConnections":4}}.

field.label: Sockopt Domain Strategy
field.help: Domain resolution strategy for the proxy server connection (stream protocols only).

field.label: Sockopt Dialer Proxy
field.help: Optional outbound tag used as dialer for this connection (chained proxy), e.g. proxy-out.

field.label: Sockopt Interface
field.help: Optional interface name to bind outbound connections to (Linux/macOS/Windows).

field.label: Sockopt Mark (SO_MARK)
field.help: Optional SO_MARK integer (Linux only, requires CAP_NET_ADMIN).

field.label: TCP Congestion Control
field.help: Optional on Linux: bbr (recommended), cubic, reno...

field.label: TCP Fast Open
field.help: Enable TCP Fast Open on the outgoing connection. Useful only if both the OS and the server support it.

field.label: TCP Keepalive Idle (s)
field.help: Optional. Seconds idle before keepalive probes start. Negative disables default keepalive.

field.label: TCP Keepalive Interval (s)
field.help: Optional. Seconds between keepalive probes. Negative disables default keepalive.

field.label: TCP User Timeout (ms)
field.help: Optional. Milliseconds before an unacknowledged TCP connection is aborted (0 or empty = disabled).

field.label: Target Strategy
field.help: How the target domain is resolved before being proxied. Applies to all protocols.

field.label: Send Through (Local IP)
field.help: Optional local IP address to bind outbound traffic to (e.g. 192.168.1.10), or 'origin'/'srcip'.

field.label: Extra HTTP Headers (JSON map)
field.help: Optional JSON object with extra headers, e.g. {"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0"}. Used by HTTP outbound and MASQUE.

field.label: Enable Mux.Cool
field.help: Multiplex several connections over one (Mux.Cool); the concurrency below sets how many. Usually off, and not compatible with the xtls-rprx-vision flow.

field.label: Mux Concurrency
field.help: Max concurrent connections per mux connection. -1 disables Mux. Default -1.

field.label: Custom StreamSettings Override (Optional JSON)
field.help: Optional JSON object merged into streamSettings (e.g. {"wsSettings":{"path":"/"}}). Outer braces are stripped; leave empty to use the UI fields above. Must be valid JSON.

field.label: TCP Mask
field.help: Last-stage camouflage for outgoing TCP. Fragment is the usual choice against SNI-based blocking; Sudoku additionally encrypts and pads the stream. Header Custom and XMC take their settings as JSON below. Only one mask can be configured here — use the raw FinalMask JSON at the end of this section to chain several masks.

field.label: Fragmented Packets
field.help: Which writes to split: tlshello fragments the TLS Client Hello, while a number or range such as 1-3 splits that many first writes of the TCP stream. Default tlshello.

field.label: Fragment Lengths (bytes)
field.help: One size or Int32 range per tag: the n-th value is the size of the n-th fragment, the last one repeats for every further fragment. Type a value and press Enter or comma to add it. Example: 3-7, 4-9, 6-9, 4-8, 5-8.

field.label: Fragment Delays (ms)
field.help: One delay or range per tag, applied before each fragment; 0 sends the next fragment immediately. With tlshello a single 0 sends the whole Client Hello as one TCP segment. Example: 30-40, 40-50, 50-60.

field.label: Max Splits
field.help: Maximum number of pieces one packet may be split into, a number or a range. 0 means unlimited. Example: 30-50.

field.label: Sudoku Password
field.help: Shared secret of the Sudoku obfuscation; the server must use the same value.

field.label: Sudoku ASCII Table
field.help: Optional custom ASCII character set used by the built-in table. Leave empty to use the default.

field.label: Sudoku Padding Min
field.help: Minimum random padding in bytes. Leave empty for the core default (0).

field.label: Sudoku Padding Max
field.help: Maximum random padding in bytes. Leave empty for the core default (0).

field.label: Sudoku Custom Tables
field.help: Optional custom tables, one per line. Leave empty to use the built-in table; a custom table must match the server.

field.label: TCP Mask Settings (JSON)
field.help: Settings object for Header Custom or XMC, copied verbatim into finalmask.tcp[0].settings. Header Custom uses clients/servers/errors arrays of packet sequences; XMC uses hostname, password and profiles. These structures are nested, so they are entered as JSON rather than rows.

field.label: UDP Mask
field.help: Last-stage camouflage for outgoing UDP. Salamander (Hysteria 2), UDP Hop and mKCP Legacy are the common choices; Noise, XDNS and Header Custom take their settings as JSON below. Only one mask can be configured here — use the raw FinalMask JSON to chain several masks.

field.label: Salamander Password
field.help: Obfuscation password, identical on the server side.

field.label: Salamander Packet Size
field.help: Optional fragment size or range (upper bound 2048), which enables Gecko obfuscation on QUIC long-header packets. Example: 512-1200.

field.label: Sudoku Password
field.help: Shared secret of the Sudoku obfuscation; the server must use the same value.

field.label: Sudoku ASCII Table
field.help: Optional custom ASCII character set used by the built-in table. Leave empty to use the default.

field.label: Sudoku Padding Min
field.help: Minimum random padding in bytes. Leave empty for the core default (0).

field.label: Sudoku Padding Max
field.help: Maximum random padding in bytes. Leave empty for the core default (0).

field.label: Sudoku Custom Tables
field.help: Optional custom tables, one per line. Leave empty to use the built-in table; a custom table must match the server.

field.label: UDP Hop Mode
field.help: Comma-separated: intervallocal, intervalremote, perconnremote. intervallocal works for WireGuard, Hysteria and XHTTP H3; the remote modes need iptables/nftables on the client. Example: intervallocal,intervalremote.

field.label: UDP Hop Interval (s)
field.help: Seconds between port changes, a number or a range. Minimum 5; the core default is 30.

field.label: UDP Hop Remote IPs
field.help: Comma-separated addresses or CIDR ranges. Required only for intervalremote/perconnremote; empty inherits the node address.

field.label: UDP Hop Remote Ports
field.help: Ports or ranges to hop between, e.g. 20000-50000,443. Required only for intervalremote/perconnremote.

field.label: mKCP Legacy Header
field.help: Fake packet header for legacy mKCP. With None, a non-empty Value is used as an AES-128-GCM password, otherwise the core falls back to simple XOR obfuscation.

field.label: mKCP Legacy Value
field.help: Password for AES-128-GCM, or the domain for the DNS header (www.baidu.com when empty). Has no effect for DTLS, SRTP, uTP, WeChat and WireGuard headers.

field.label: XICMP Datagram Mode
field.help: Use datagram ICMP sockets, which need fewer privileges. Client-side only; supported on Linux, macOS and iOS.

field.label: XICMP IPs
field.help: Optional comma-separated IP addresses the ICMP traffic may use. CIDR is not supported by XICMP.

field.label: Realm URL
field.help: realm://token@host[:port]/id (or realm+http://...) issued by a hysteria-realm server.

field.label: Realm STUN Servers
field.help: Comma-separated STUN servers as host:port, used for NAT port prediction. At least one is required.

field.label: Realm IP Mode
field.help: Controls STUN name resolution and peer filtering, e.g. dual. Leave empty for the core default.

field.label: UDP Mask Settings (JSON)
field.help: Settings object for Noise, XDNS or Header Custom, copied verbatim into finalmask.udp[0].settings. Noise uses reset and a noise array; XDNS uses domains and resolvers; Header Custom uses client and server arrays. These structures are nested, so they are entered as JSON rather than rows.

field.label: QUIC Congestion Control
field.help: Congestion control for QUIC transports (XHTTP H3, Hysteria, MASQUE H3). Hysteria defaults to Brutal, XHTTP H3 and MASQUE to BBR. XHTTP H3 cannot use Brutal, only Force Brutal.

field.label: BBR Profile
field.help: Preset used when the congestion control is BBR. Default is Standard.

field.label: Brutal Up Rate
field.help: Upload rate, e.g. 20 mbps. Direction is relative to this client: your upload is the server's download. 0 or empty means BBR instead of Brutal. Force Brutal requires a value.

field.label: Brutal Down Rate
field.help: Download rate, e.g. 100 mbps. 0 or empty means no limit.

field.label: Max Idle Timeout (s)
field.help: How long the peer waits without data before closing the QUIC connection. 4 to 120 seconds; the core default is 30.

field.label: KeepAlive Period (s)
field.help: QUIC KeepAlive interval, 2 to 60 seconds. Disabled by default.

field.label: Max Incoming Streams
field.help: Server-side limit for concurrent QUIC streams. When set it must be at least 8.

field.label: Initial Stream Window
field.help: Initial QUIC stream receive window in bytes, at least 16384. Leave empty unless you know what you are doing; keep the stream-to-connection window ratio near 2:5.

field.label: Max Stream Window
field.help: Maximum QUIC stream receive window in bytes, at least 16384. Leave empty unless you know what you are doing.

field.label: Initial Connection Window
field.help: Initial QUIC connection receive window in bytes, at least 16384. Leave empty unless you know what you are doing.

field.label: Max Connection Window
field.help: Maximum QUIC connection receive window in bytes, at least 16384. Leave empty unless you know what you are doing.

field.label: Disable Path MTU Discovery
field.help: Turn off QUIC Path MTU Discovery. Useful on operating systems the core does not auto-tune (FreeBSD is not in that list), so enable it if QUIC connections stall.

field.label: Raw FinalMask JSON (override)
field.help: Optional. When this object is not empty it replaces everything configured in the rows above, which is the only way to chain several masks (finalmask.tcp and finalmask.udp are arrays, the first entry is the innermost layer) or to configure filter masks. Clear it to let the rows build the object.
